feature_topics.rationale: Use public AppKit glass for an editable omnibox and native navigation, retaining Chromium extension/menu controls in a child widget. Honor profile appearance with OS fallback, standard traffic-light spacing, 48 pt hover retention, native dragging and sidebar menus. The current macOS frame uses a 16 pt perimeter, edge-to-edge content, a flush square full-width glass sidebar, a pinned semantic separator, and a 52 pt header with 36 pt controls and 8 pt outer insets. Reveal uses 8 pt windowed bands and 4 top/1 side physical pixels fullscreen. Both sidebar modes follow the fullscreen menu bar. Native hit routing preserves window resizing; live resize retains existing header/sidebar presentation. Shut down autocomplete before profile teardown. Use the existing synchronous Chromium resize path and remove unsuccessful custom cursor tracking and sidebar-coordinate workarounds; cursor flicker remains unresolved and is deferred in GitHub issue #5. Fade trailing toolbar contents instead of NSWindow alpha, which Chromium owns for compositor visibility. Keep the sidebar toggle within its sidebar and preserve tab interactions, inner-edge resizing, theme semantics and customization panel input exclusions. Retain already revealed chrome for the native green-button menu using its owning button remote-view lifecycle and in-process menu tracking fallback.
feature_topics.adaptation: Locally authored reusable macOS feature, separate from distribution branding; see agent-docs/project/features/floating-address-bar.md for the desktop design reference and validation limits. Native window-menu retention checks the remote helper running flag because AppKit can cache an idle attached helper.

policy: Reviewed ports are already composed into the locked platform commit and verified against series order and SHA-256. Builds never download a moving PR patch or replay an unreviewed head. Chromium upgrades take priority over UI parity; no downgrade to satisfy optional patches.
